 THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL IS FILED UNDER  SECTION 173(1) OF THE MOTOR VEHICLE ACT 1988, AGAINST THE  JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED: 03.03.2011 PASSED IN MVC  NO.290/2010 ON THE FILE OF THE PRESIDING OFFICER, FAST  TRACK COURT-IV, BELAGAVI AT BELAGAVI, DISMISSING THE  PETITION FILED UNDER SECTION 166 OF MOTOR VEHICLES ACT.
 -2-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:1153  MFA No. 21874 of 2011  THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Heard Sri.Madanmohan M Khannur, learned counsel for the appellant and Smt.Anusha Sangami,
learned counsel for respondent - Insurance Company.
2.

The present appeal is filed by the claimant in MVC No.290/2010 challenging the validity of the judgment and award dated 03.03.2011 passed by the Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Belagavi whereby the claim petition came to be dismissed.

entities.text:
Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Belagavi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
3. Facts in brief which are utmost necessary for disposal of this case are as under:
3.1 A claim petition came to be filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act contending that on 09.01.2010 the claimant was proceeding on motorcycle bearing No.KA-22/EC-7768 from Basurte towards Bachi village via Uchagaon to attend electrical work at Basurte village and when he reached near Basurte cross in front of D.Ed.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:1153 college on Uchagaon-Kowad road at 5.30 p.m., a car came from opposite side in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle and in order to avoid the accident the rider of the motorcycle suddenly and abruptly applied the break whereby motorcycle got skid and toppled down.
As a result, the claimant sustained injuries and he was shifted to Aadhar hospital, Belagavi and he took treatment as inpatient.

During the said period, the owner of the vehicle and rider of the motorcycle requested the claimant not to lodge complaint and therefore he did not lodge complaint on the ground that there was promise to settle the compensation.
Doctors of Aadhar hospital therefore did not prepare MLC records and did not intimate the police.

Gurunath S/O Ningappa Waghulkar vs Prakash S/O Durgappa Koravi on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152912114/
2 3.2

It is further contended that before discharge from the hospital, Prakash Durgappa Koravi who is the owner of the motorcycle came there and paid a sum of Rs.10,000/- and promised to pay the balance amount.
But he failed to keep up his promise.
Therefore, the claimant filed a claim petition.
3.3 Upon receipt of notice of the claim petition, both the respondents appeared before the Tribunal and have filed objection statements denying the claim petition averments in toto.
3.4 In view of rival contentions, the Tribunal raised the following issues:

1 Whether the petitioner proves that on 09/01/2010 at about 5-30 p.m., near Basurte cross in front of D.Ed college, on Uchagaon Kowad Road, Tq. & Dist.
Belgaum, the accident had taken place due to the rash and negligent riding of Motor cycle bearing No. KA-22/EC-7768 by its rider and thus he was injured?
2. Whether the Respondent No.2 proves that the rider of the motor cycle was not holding a valid driving licence at the time of accident?
3. Whether the Respondent No.2 proves that this Court has no jurisdiction to try this case?
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom?
5.
What order or award?
3.5 In order to prove the claim petition averments, the claimant got examined himself as PW.1 and placed on record six documents which were exhibited and marked as Exs.P.1 to P.6.
He also examined one Dattatray Sutar and Dr.A.B.Patil as witnesses on his behalf as PW.2 and PW.3.
3.6 As against the evidence placed on record, officer of the Insurance Company namely Harish Jadhav has been examined as RW.1 and he has placed on record insurance policy at Ex.R.1.

3.7 The Tribunal on cumulative consideration of the oral and documentary evidence placed on record, recorded a categorical finding that the claimant failed to prove that he sustained the alleged injuries mentioned in disability certificate marked at Ex.P.4 in the road traffic accident NC:
2024:KHC-D:1153 that occurred on 09.01.2010 involving motorcycle bearing No.KA-22/EC-7768 and dismissed the claim petition.
4. Being aggrieved by the same, the claimant has preferred the present appeal.

Gurunath S/O Ningappa Waghulkar vs Prakash S/O Durgappa Koravi on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152912114/
3

5. Reiterating the grounds urged in the appeal memorandum, Sri.Madanmohan M Khannur, learned counsel for the appellant - claimant vehemently contended that the Tribunal has grossly erred in not appreciating the case of the claimant in its proper perspective and dismissed the claim petition resulting in miscarriage of justice and sought for allowing the appeal.
6. Per contra, Smt.Anusha Sangami, learned counsel representing the Insurance Company supported the impugned judgment.
7. In view of the rival contentions of the parties, this Court perused the material on record meticulously.

Having perused the material on record, the following points would arise for consideration:
NC: 2024:KHC-D:1153 i.

Whether the appellant - claimant has made out a case that he sustained injuries mentioned in the disability certificate at Ex.P.4 in respect of a road traffic accident occurred on 09.01.2010 at about 5.30 p.m. in front of D.Ed college on Uchagaon-Kowad road involving motorcycle bearing No.KA-22/EC-7768?

ii. If so, whether the claimant would be entitled for compensation and to what extent?
iii.Whether the impugned judgment and award is suffering from legal infirmity and perversity and thus calls for interference?
iv. What order?

[ Reg. Point Nos.1 to 3:
8.
In the case on hand, the claimant has admittedly not filed any police complaint nor doctors who treated him in Aadhar hospital have sent any MLC report to the jurisdictional police.
Ex.P.1 is the medical certificate issued by the doctor to establish that claimant has sustained injuries.
Ex.P.2 is the hospital bill, Ex.P.3 is X- NC: 2024:KHC-D:1153 ray bill, Ex.P.4 is the disability certificate and Ex.P.5 and Ex.P.6 are the X-ray report and original X-ray film.
9. The claimant has reiterated the contents of the complaint/petition averments in his examination-in-chief.
He has admitted that he has been shifted to Aadhar hospital on the next day of alleged accident.
Soon after accident, he has consulted Dr.Kadam on the date of accident in Uchagaon.
He has answered that his uncle has taken him to Dr.Kadam's hospital.
He admits that he has taken treatment initially with Dr.Bamani for a period of two months.
He answered that Dr.Bamani has treated him in Aadhar hospital.
He admits that in Ex.P.1 it has been mentioned that case has been referred by Dr.Bamani.
He admits that there is no impediment for him to obtain a certificate from Dr.Bamani.
He has also answered that he has mentioned Dr.Kadam about the injuries sustained by him in the alleged road traffic accident.

Gurunath S/O Ningappa Waghulkar vs Prakash S/O Durgappa Koravi on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152912114/
4 10.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: PW.2 is uncle of claimant who admitted him to Aadhar hospital.
He also admits that there was no NC: 2024:KHC-D:1153 impediment for him to lodge a complaint.
However, he has answered that since the injured was being shifted to hospital, he did not lodge complaint.

11. PW.3 in his cross-examination has stated that the injured has visited him for obtaining the disability certificate and he examined records and issued disability certificate and what has been recorded by him in the disability certificate is based on the records produced before him and the oral statement made by the injured/claimant.
12. The above evidence is re-appreciated by this Court in this appeal in view of the grounds urged in the appeal memorandum.

13. On such re-appreciation, it is crystal clear that PW.1 himself has admitted that he has taken treatment with Dr.Kadam at the first instance and thereafter with Dr.Bamani and admitted to Aadhar hospital.

Pertinently, neither Dr.Kadam nor Dr.Bamani has been examined as witness on behalf of claimant to establish that he had immediately got treated with those doctors with regard to the alleged road traffic accident.
15.

In the absence of MLC report or complaint given by Dr.Kadam or Dr.Bamani or for that matter by Aadhar hospital, the trial Court has disbelieved the case of the claimant that he has sustained the injuries mentioned in the medical certificate and disability certificate on account of road traffic accident involving motorcycle bearing No.KA-22/EC-7768.
16.
As such, even after re-appreciation of entire material on record, this Court does not find legal infirmity or perversity in recording the said finding by the Tribunal.
Accordingly, point Nos.1 to 3 are answered in negative.

Reg. Point No.4:
17.

In view of findings on point Nos.1 to 3, following order is passed:
- 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:1153 ORDER
(i) Appeal is meritless and is hereby dismissed.
(ii) No order as to costs.
